standard_prerequisites.name: A complex that is m-pseudo-coherent relative to a base remains so when it is viewed as a complex over a larger polynomial algebra over the same base, provided the algebra used is pseudo-coherent as a module over that larger algebra
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 21515-21518 and again at proof lines 21535-21539
standard_prerequisites.use: Moves relative pseudo-coherence from the localized base to a polynomial ring over the base and then to the quotient presenting the further localization.

standard_prerequisites.name: The localization of a ring at an element is the quotient of a polynomial ring by the relation expressing the inverse of that element, and the same holds for a second localization
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the explicit presentations in terms of which the two moves are made.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pulling back a relatively pseudo-coherent complex along a ring map of finite presentation preserves relative pseudo-coherence
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the tensor product of the complex with the localization of the polynomial algebra with the complex over the localized algebra.

core_obligations: Rewrite the localized base ring as the quotient of a polynomial ring in one variable by the relation making the element invertible, and choose a surjection from a polynomial algebra over the localized base onto the algebra (proof lines 21508-21511).

Conclude from the surjection that the complex is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex over the polynomial algebra over the base, using that the polynomial algebra over the localized base is pseudo-coherent as a module over that larger polynomial algebra (proof lines 21511-21518).

Choose a lift of the element to the polynomial algebra over the base, use the pullback statement to identify the tensor product of the complex with the localization of that polynomial algebra with the complex over the localized algebra, and conclude relative pseudo-coherence over the polynomial algebra localized at the lift (proof lines 21519-21530).

Rewrite that localization as a quotient of a polynomial ring in one further variable by the relation making the lift invertible, and apply the same transfer of relative pseudo-coherence to obtain that the complex over the further local algebra is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex over the polynomial ring over the base, which is the assertion of the lemma (proof lines 21531-21539).
proof_roadmap: Present the localized base ring as a quotient of a polynomial ring and lift the finiteness of the algebra to the polynomial algebra over the base (proof lines 21508-21518).
Localize at a lift of the element and use pullback of relative pseudo-coherence (proof lines 21519-21530).
Present the second localization as a further quotient and transfer relative pseudo-coherence once more (proof lines 21531-21539).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that a complex that is m-pseudo-coherent relative to the localization of a ring at an element stays so after localizing the algebra at a further element, now relative to the original ring (statement lines 21498-21505). The proof is a two-step transfer: it first expresses the localized base ring as a quotient of a polynomial ring so that relative pseudo-coherence can be moved to a polynomial algebra over the base, then localizes at a lift of the element using the pullback statement, and finally presents that second localization as one more quotient and transfers relative pseudo-coherence once more (proof lines 21507-21539). The two transfers and the two presentations are what make the change of base from the localization to the original ring work. The counted span refers twice to earlier results of this chapter, both carried as navigation stubs.
